authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Operative - Formal Execution.md, §XVI (The Token Inside the Gate); Capstone §VI.1 duty 3
note: SPEC vectors, not parity vectors. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: The reference Python engine has NO approval token. `approval_token`, `valid_token` and `effect_class` are grep-0 in apps/api/sustena/ — re-confirmed at the time of writing, and independently recorded by the Operative article's own Sustena Note. So `replayed_by` is ["rust"] alone, and that is a deliberate, documented divergence rather than a silent one.
divergence.python_behaviour_today: In Python, 'the human decides' holds by structural incapacity plus a single human-mediated route (core/advisory.py cannot act; accept_suggestion() routes through execute_operator; egress needs a separate confirm_egress). Same destination, different mechanism, narrower coverage — it is policy plus incapacity, not complete mediation.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged. Nothing here is Rust-specific: the behaviour is the article's.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. Every pre-existing vector runs with effect_class = unchecked and is byte-identical to before this slice.

trace_cases.name: the_only_route_to_a_token_is_sim_then_vote_then_approve
trace_cases.why: §XVI's trace invariant: ∀ live e: ∃ e_sim ≺ e_vote ≺ e_approve ≺ e. It is prefix-closed, hence a safety property, hence enforceable — so it is built as structure. In Rust the stages consume each other by value and ApprovalToken has no public constructor, so a skipped stage is not expressible. This case records the behaviour a host in another language must reproduce.

trace_cases.name: a_refused_simulation_cannot_be_voted_on
trace_cases.why: A simulation the gate refused has nothing to approve. The chain stops at the first stage.

trace_cases.name: only_a_passed_proposal_can_be_approved
trace_cases.why: The council advises; a proposal still in voting is not a decision.

trace_cases.name: a_deadline_passing_is_not_an_approval
trace_cases.why: DEFERRED means the deadline passed with no human decision. Never an auto-approval — the one place a timeout must not become a yes.

trace_cases.name: a_failed_proposal_cannot_be_approved
trace_cases.why: The council produced no votes at all.

validation_cases.name: an_approval_binds_to_an_act_not_a_shape_of_act__amount
validation_cases.why: §XVI, verbatim: 'yes, pay the rent' must not admit a different amount to a different payee. This is the case the whole binding exists for.

validation_cases.name: an_approval_binds_to_an_act_not_a_shape_of_act__payee
validation_cases.why: The other half of the same sentence.

validation_cases.name: a_token_for_one_operator_does_not_admit_another
validation_cases.why: Same parameters, different act. 'WrongAct' and 'WrongParams' are separate answers because they call for different things from the person.

validation_cases.name: one_persons_approval_does_not_admit_anothers_act
validation_cases.why: The token names who approved. Another member's authority to act is not authority to spend this approval.

validation_cases.name: expiry_is_inclusive
validation_cases.why: A boundary worth pinning: at exactly the expiry the approval still holds.

validation_cases.name: an_expired_approval_is_refused
validation_cases.why: §XVI: expiring, with re-admission at commit — the state at approval time need not be the state at commit time.

validation_cases.name: parameter_order_is_not_part_of_the_act
validation_cases.why: The binding is over the parameter MAP, not its serialisation. Two hosts that order keys differently must reach the same verdict, or the token is an artefact of how a request was written down.

single_use_cases.name: an_approval_is_single_use
single_use_cases.why: §XVI: delivery is at-least-once and the record dedupes on stable ids, so a replayable approval is one you gave once and spent twice.

single_use_cases.name: a_ledger_restored_from_the_host_still_refuses_a_replay
single_use_cases.why: A process restart is not a way to spend an approval twice. Single-use is a property of the record, not of one process's memory.

single_use_cases.name: distinct_approvals_do_not_collide
single_use_cases.why: Spending one approval must not invalidate an unrelated one.

gate_cases.name: a_live_effect_with_a_matching_approval_commits
gate_cases.why: The whole clause, end to end, through the real gate.

gate_cases.name: an_unapproved_live_effect_is_not_a_move
gate_cases.why: §XVI's closing form: an unapproved live effect is not blocked, penalised, or flagged for review — there is no admitted operator application that produces it. In Rust it is not even expressible (EffectClass::Live carries the token), so this case records the ONLY reachable near-miss: an approval that does not match the act.

gate_cases.name: a_sandbox_effect_needs_no_approval
gate_cases.why: effect_class = sandbox satisfies the disjunction on its own. Operative §X's fork-and-replay.

gate_cases.name: a_sandbox_effect_is_exempt_from_the_token_not_from_the_gate
gate_cases.why: The sandbox is bounded by exactly the household's own law: a fork can never reach a state the real Sustain would refuse. Exempting simulation from the INVARIANTS is how a fork becomes a second write path.

gate_cases.name: a_refused_call_does_not_burn_the_approval
gate_cases.why: Being turned back by a guard should leave the person free to fix the state and use the same approval. The nonce is spent at commit and nowhere else.

gate_cases.name: a_replayed_live_effect_is_refused_and_changes_nothing
gate_cases.why: The same approval, delivered twice. The first commits; the second must not.
